power-platform-dataflows.title: Overview of dataflows across Power Platform and Dynamics 365 – Microsoft Learn
power-platform-dataflows.notes: Dataflows are a self-service, cloud-based data preparation technology built on Power Query. They load, transform and store data in Microsoft Dataverse, in a Power BI workspace or in an organization's Azure Data Lake Storage account. The documentation lists more than 80 supported data sources, and a dataflow can run on demand or on a schedule. Their purpose is to keep transformation logic in one central place, separate from the modeling and visualization layer in Power BI, so that several solutions can reuse the same prepared tables. Other services such as Power BI, Power Apps, Power Automate and Dynamics 365 applications read the results through Dataverse, the dataflow connector or the lake. Typical scenarios include migrating legacy data into Dataverse, replacing ETL tooling when building a data warehouse or star schema, and avoiding duplicated Power Query code across reports. No dataflow-specific license is required, since the feature is covered by the licensing of Power Apps, Power BI or Dynamics 365 Customer Insights. On-premises sources need an on-premises data gateway. Power BI dataflow Gen1 is described as legacy and gets no new features, while Gen2 is recommended for Premium customers with Fabric access.

privileged-identity-management.title: What is Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management? – Microsoft Learn
privileged-identity-management.notes: Privileged Identity Management is a service in Microsoft Entra ID for managing, controlling and monitoring access to important resources in Entra ID, Azure, Microsoft 365 and Intune. Its goal is to reduce the number of people holding sensitive access and to provide just-in-time elevation to privileged roles. Assignments can be eligible, meaning the user must activate the role before use, or active, meaning the rights are available immediately; both can be time-bound or permanent. Features include start and end dates, approval workflows for activation, multifactor authentication on each activation, a required justification, notifications, access reviews and downloadable audit history. The service also protects against removing the last active Global Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator. Management covers Entra roles, Azure resource roles and PIM for Groups, with Microsoft Graph APIs for programmatic access. Using the service requires licenses, which the page leaves to the Entra ID Governance licensing documentation.

purview-unified-catalog.title: Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog – Microsoft Learn
purview-unified-catalog.notes: The Unified Catalog is the data governance platform within Microsoft Purview, described as an integrated software-as-a-service framework built on an inventory of data assets with their metadata and lineage. It supports data discovery, secure access, curation by owners and stewards, measurement of governance health and the linking of data to business goals. The approach is federated governance, with central standards and responsibilities held in the business units. Main building blocks are governance domains that group data by business concept, data products that bundle tables, files or Power BI reports for a use case, glossary terms, critical data elements, and objectives and key results. Health controls score the governance state and health actions suggest improvements. Data quality rules and scores exist for domains, data products and assets, and access policies let users request access to data products. Users can search or browse the catalog and use an AI-based copilot. Using the new experience requires upgrading to the enterprise version of the new Purview experience, which is being rolled out gradually by environment and region, so it is not yet available everywhere. Numeric limits and pricing are left to linked articles.

quantum-development-kit.title: Microsoft Quantum Development Kit overview – Microsoft Learn
quantum-development-kit.notes: The Quantum Development Kit is a free, open-source toolkit for writing, simulating, debugging and running quantum programs. It connects to Azure Quantum, so programs can be executed on real quantum computers in the cloud. The documentation organizes it into a core foundation, productivity tooling and domain-specific libraries. Described capabilities include support for the Q# and OpenQASM languages, quantum simulators with noise models, a circuit editor, a resource estimator, quantum error correction and Copilot integration in Visual Studio Code. A separate chemistry library targets chemistry and materials science work, and learning material is part of the offering. The kit ships as three components: an extension for Visual Studio Code from the marketplace, a qdk Python package and a qdk-chemistry Python library, both from PyPI. They can be used individually or combined, for example by writing a Q# or OpenQASM program in VS Code and then importing it into Python to estimate resources. The overview page gives only the description free and open source as licensing information and points to separate installation guides. It does not list system requirements, hardware providers, qubit counts or the cost of hardware runs.

standard-channels.title: Standard channels in Microsoft Teams – Microsoft Learn
standard-channels.notes: A standard channel in Microsoft Teams is visible and accessible to every member of a team, including invited guests, and serves collaboration around a topic, project or department. Typical uses are group discussions, project updates, file sharing, announcements, knowledge sharing and social topics. Every team has a General channel that stays at the top of the channel list and suits announcements and general conversation. Conversations and shared files can be searched within a channel and across teams. All standard channels of a team use the same SharePoint site, a Teams-connected site, where each channel appears as a folder in the document library and the Files tab maps to that folder. Standard channels differ from private channels, which only reach explicitly added members and guests, and from shared channels, which include channel members and B2B direct connect users across teams. Permissions depend on the role: owners can create or delete channels, add members, edit names and descriptions and manage tabs and apps, while members can do some of these if the owner enables it and guests only if an admin enables it in Entra ID. The page names no licenses or numeric limits and points to private channels for sensitive content.

teams-app-manifest.title: Microsoft 365 app manifest schema reference – Microsoft Learn
teams-app-manifest.notes: The app manifest, formerly called the Teams app manifest, is a JSON file that describes an app's functionality and configuration and defines how it integrates with Microsoft 365 products such as Copilot, Teams and Outlook. It is part of the unified Microsoft 365 app package, a ZIP archive holding the manifest, icons and optional Copilot agent manifests. The format is used to submit declarative agents, Teams apps, SharePoint Framework apps, Graph connectors and Office add-ins, either as a store offering through Partner Center or directly to an organization's catalog, and the apps are then managed under Integrated Apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The version history shows how the schema grows: properties such as bots with commands, static tabs and compose extensions exist alongside newer ones like copilotAgents, agentConnectors for MCP servers, agentSkills, activity icons and keyboard shortcuts. Some limits are stated, for example bot commands were raised from ten to twelve, and the properties packageName and callingSidePanel are deprecated. Combining Copilot agents with Office add-ins is still in preview. The page itself names no license or prerequisite information.

virtual-network-service-endpoints.title: Virtual Network service endpoints overview – Microsoft Learn
virtual-network-service-endpoints.notes: Virtual network service endpoints give a subnet direct, private access to selected Azure services over the Azure backbone, so resources in the subnet can reach those services without public IP addresses. After an endpoint is enabled on a subnet, a virtual network rule on the target service restricts access to that network, which removes public internet access to the resource. Endpoints are switched on per subnet and per service, and several services can be combined on one subnet. Related building blocks include service tags in network security groups, service endpoint policies that filter access to specific resources, and routes with the next hop type VirtualNetworkServiceEndpoint that take precedence over BGP and user-defined routes. Supported services include Storage, SQL Database, Cosmos DB, Key Vault, Service Bus, Event Hubs, App Service and Container Registry. No extra charge applies, and a special permission on the subnet is needed. Endpoints do not cover traffic from on-premises, the source address changes from public to private IPv4, and DNS records still resolve to public addresses. Microsoft recommends Private Link and private endpoints as the preferred option.

viva-glint.title: Viva Glint programs, survey types, and templates – Microsoft Learn
viva-glint.notes: Viva Glint is a solution for employee surveys and listening, built around frequent feedback that organizations turn into concrete improvements. The documentation defines engagement as the degree to which employees direct their cognitive, emotional and behavioral energy toward positive organizational goals. The technology is configurable rather than a fixed formula, and the Microsoft people science team updates survey items and templates. There are four program types: recurring or special topic programs that allow trend comparison, employee lifecycle programs triggered by hire or exit dates, ad hoc programs for a single occasion, and always-on programs that can be answered at any time. Every type offers ready-made templates and a blank one, and only templates with cycles can recur. Listed templates include engagement, onboarding, exit, productivity, culture, diversity and inclusion, manager effectiveness and team effectiveness. Administrators set the survey rhythm, several surveys can run in parallel, and the page points to survey fatigue as a concern. Six introduction email templates support rollout. Licensing and numeric limits are not covered on this page.

windows-365-frontline.title: Windows 365 Flex (formerly Frontline) – Microsoft Windows 365
windows-365-frontline.notes: The product page now presents Windows 365 Flex, formerly named Frontline, as a way to stream secure Cloud PC access to shift workers by sharing licenses among several users. It targets employees and contractors who need a Cloud PC only during scheduled working time, such as shift, seasonal or part-time staff. Two modes exist. In dedicated mode, one license allows up to three personalized Cloud PCs that keep apps, data and settings, but only one is active at a time. In shared mode, one license maps to one Cloud PC that several users take in turn, never at once, and administrators control personalization. Cloud Apps deliver single applications instead of a full desktop, run only in shared mode, are managed through Intune and are reached through the Windows App. License requirements follow those of Windows 365 Enterprise, and the number of licenses per policy depends on peak concurrent use. Users who need access at any time are better served by Windows 365 Enterprise, according to the FAQ. Concrete prices are left to a separate pricing page.

windows-app.title: What is Windows App? – Microsoft Learn
windows-app.notes: Windows App is an application for securely connecting remotely to Windows devices and apps. It supports Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365 Cloud PCs, Microsoft Dev Box, Remote Desktop Services and remote PCs. Platforms include Windows, macOS, iOS and iPadOS, Android and Chrome OS, web browsers and Meta Quest. Support differs by target: in a web browser, Remote Desktop Services and remote PC connections are not available, and on Windows the separate Remote Desktop app is used for Remote Desktop Services. Features include a customizable home screen with pinned favorites, access to several services from one interface, switching between accounts, multiple monitors, dynamic resolution and scaling, redirection of webcams, audio, storage and printers, and optimizations for Microsoft Teams. Signing in is required for Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365, Dev Box and Remote Desktop Services, using a work or school account supplied by an administrator, while personal Microsoft accounts are not allowed. Remote PC connections work without signing in. The browser version needs no installation. The page lists no licensing details for the target services.

azure-dns.title: Azure DNS overview: hosting and resolution – Microsoft Learn
azure-dns.notes: Azure DNS provides DNS hosting, name resolution and load balancing for applications on Azure infrastructure, covering both public internet domains and private zones. Azure Public DNS hosts domains and lets administrators manage records with the same credentials, APIs, tools and billing as other Azure services. Azure Private DNS manages and resolves names inside virtual networks without a custom DNS solution. Azure DNS Private Resolver allows queries from on-premises environments to private zones and the reverse, without VM-based DNS servers. DNS Resolver Policy filters and logs DNS queries at virtual network level and includes a threat intelligence feed, so known malicious domains can be blocked from resolution. Azure Traffic Manager is a DNS-based traffic load balancer, but it is a separate service with its own documentation. Scenarios named on the page include hosting public domains, automatic registration of VMs, name resolution between Azure and on-premises, monitoring through metrics and alerts, protection of zones and records, and failover. Azure DNS belongs to the network foundations category together with virtual networks and Private Link. Prerequisites, prices and limits are not stated and are left to the FAQ pages.

azure-open-datasets.title: What are open datasets? Curated public datasets – Microsoft Learn
azure-open-datasets.notes: Azure Open Datasets are curated public datasets on Azure that can be added to machine learning solutions as scenario-specific features to obtain more accurate models. They contain public-domain data on weather, census, holidays, public safety and location. The data is copied into the Azure cloud and reloaded from its sources at regular intervals, for example from NOAA over FTP, then parsed into a structured format and enriched where needed, such as with ZIP codes or the locations of the nearest weather stations. Datasets sit alongside cloud compute to ease access and processing. They integrate with Azure Machine Learning through the UI and SDK, with Azure Databricks and with notebooks, and can be reached through APIs, Power BI and Azure Data Factory. Users can also share their own public datasets. Examples include New York taxi trip records, US labor force statistics and US employment, hours and earnings data. Access works with an Azure account, but the Python package azureml-opendatasets can also be used in any Python environment, with or without Spark, without an account. The page gives no prices, service levels or usage limits and does not specify the refresh intervals.

azure-sphere.title: Azure Sphere documentation – Microsoft Learn
azure-sphere.notes: Azure Sphere is described as a comprehensive IoT solution made of a secured, connected microcontroller, a custom Linux-based operating system and a cloud-based security service. The documentation is organized around developing applications, managing devices and deployments, and designing and manufacturing connected devices. Hardware material includes development kits and a reference board design published on GitHub. The cloud side is the Azure Sphere Security Service, which has its own REST API reference. Developers can build high-level applications, real-time applications and partner applications for multicore chips, and they work with the Azure Sphere CLI. Integration topics include Azure IoT, Azure role-based access control for resources, Azure Monitor and diagnostic data collection, and the cloud-based deployment of applications. For manufacturing, the pages cover factory floor procedures and preparing connected devices for shipment with the right cloud configuration. The page also compares the integrated version of Azure Sphere with the legacy version and notes that the Azure Sphere Gallery is no longer maintained. It states no licensing prerequisites, quotas or costs.

cloud-pki.title: Microsoft Cloud PKI for Intune overview – Microsoft Learn
cloud-pki.notes: Microsoft Cloud PKI is a cloud service that automates the certificate lifecycle for devices managed by Intune. It provides a dedicated public key infrastructure for the organization without on-premises servers, connectors or hardware, and it handles issuing, renewing and revoking certificates on all platforms Intune supports. Certificates serve scenarios such as VPN, Wi-Fi, email, web and device identity, and the service can replace an on-premises certification authority, NDES and the Intune certificate connector. A two-tier hierarchy of root and issuing CA is created in the cloud, and a bring-your-own-CA option links an Intune issuing CA to a private CA such as AD CS. Devices receive trust and SCEP profiles, generate a certificate signing request so the private key never leaves the device, and get the signed certificate back. Intune hosts the CRL and AIA endpoints, and a dashboard reports active, expired and revoked certificates. Role-based access control and scope tags apply. A Cloud PKI add-on is needed on top of Intune Plan 1 or 2, either in the Intune Suite or as a standalone license. A tenant may hold at most three CAs, trial CAs use software keys, and the data residency option is not currently available.

adaptive-card-designer.title: Adaptive Cards Designer SDK – Microsoft Learn
adaptive-card-designer.notes: The Adaptive Cards Designer is an interactive, design-time surface for authoring Adaptive Cards. It runs in the browser, so cards can be designed without a local development environment. The documentation describes a software development kit that allows the designer to be embedded in a custom web application, which lets users build cards without leaving that application for the external designer page. The component is distributed as the npm package adaptivecards-designer, and it can alternatively be loaded as a script from a content delivery network. The package itself holds the complete documentation for the SDK. A related tools page mentions a JSON schema for Adaptive Cards that supports validation and IntelliSense in Visual Studio and VS Code, although it does not say whether the designer uses that schema. The pages list no individual designer functions beyond authoring cards, and they name no prerequisites for browser use, no license terms, no costs and no known limits. Embedding requires a web application and the npm package.

agent-identity-blueprint.title: Agent identity blueprint – Microsoft Learn
agent-identity-blueprint.notes: An agent identity blueprint is an object in Microsoft Entra ID that acts as a template for agent identities and defines how agents are created, authenticated and managed. It works as a container, so many agent identities of one kind can be administered centrally while each keeps its own identity, credentials and permissions. Shared properties include a description, app roles, the verified publisher and authentication protocol settings such as optional claims. Credentials for requesting access tokens are configured on the blueprint, and OAuth permissions granted to it apply to every identity created from it. Conditional Access policies applied to the blueprint reach all its agent identities, and disabling the blueprint stops authentication for all of them. A blueprint is also an identity itself, with one allowed operation, which is provisioning or deprovisioning agent identities. For that it needs an OAuth client ID, credentials and the Graph permission AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager, and it is created through Microsoft Graph. Required resource access and inheritable permissions are only declarations, so administrators must still give consent. Blueprints can be single-tenant or multitenant. No licensing requirements are named.

api-management-developer-portal.title: Overview of the developer portal – Azure API Management – Microsoft Learn
api-management-developer-portal.notes: The developer portal of Azure API Management is an automatically generated, customizable website that documents the APIs of an instance, so consumers can discover them, learn how to use them, request access and try them out. An integrated visual editor lets publishers add, remove and move pages, sections and widgets and adjust fonts and colors, and visibility of pages, menus and buttons can be controlled by user group. An interactive test console supports APIs without authorization, with subscription keys or with OAuth 2.0, and needs a CORS policy on the APIs. Signed-in users see reports on their own usage, response times and data volume. Sign-in is anonymous by default, with optional basic authentication, Microsoft Entra ID, Entra External ID or delegation. Changes become visible only after publishing, each publish is stored as a revision, and earlier revisions can be restored. Extensions include a custom HTML widget, custom widgets and a WordPress plugin, and the portal can be self-hosted, though visibility controls exist only in the managed portal and support covers just the basic setup. It applies to the Developer, Basic, Standard and Premium tiers and their v2 variants, and the Consumption tier is not mentioned.

api-plugins.title: API plugins for Microsoft 365 Copilot – Microsoft Learn
api-plugins.notes: API plugins are custom actions that let declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot work with REST APIs that have an OpenAPI description. They are not standalone installable packages, and only the agent that contains a plugin can use its functions. Users can ask in natural language to query data and, if the API allows it, to create, update or delete data. Copilot reads a plugin manifest to discover the API and picks an operation based on the OpenAPI operation and parameter descriptions. Adaptive Card templates in the manifest shape how results are displayed, and citation metadata can be taken from the response. If the API needs authentication, the plugin gets a token or key from a token store, and the agent asks the user to sign in when needed. Copilot asks for consent on first use, after which read operations run without confirmation while write operations still ask, and developers can override these defaults. The API itself is hosted outside Microsoft 365. Up to five plugins in an agent manifest are always added to the prompt, and beyond that a semantic selection by plugin description applies. Quality can drop from about ten functions, and the token window truncates large inputs and outputs. No licensing requirements are named.

automatic-attack-disruption.title: Automatic attack disruption in Microsoft Defender XDR – Microsoft Learn
automatic-attack-disruption.notes: Automatic attack disruption is a capability built into Microsoft Defender XDR that detects ongoing attacks and automatically contains affected assets. It assesses the whole attack at incident level rather than single indicators of compromise. The aim is to limit lateral movement early, reduce the impact of an attack and give the security team time to remediate fully, while the team keeps control of investigation and recovery and every automatic action can be undone. It works in three stages: signals from endpoints, identities, email and collaboration and SaaS apps are correlated into a high-confidence incident, the assets under attacker control are identified, and response actions are run in the relevant Defender products. Actions include containing or isolating a device, containing or disabling a user, revoking sessions in Microsoft Entra ID and handling OAuth app compromise. Predictive shielding applies protective measures such as hardening in advance. Okta and AWS IAM integrations are in preview. Containment applies to devices onboarded to Defender for Endpoint, and disabling Active Directory accounts relies on domain controllers with the Defender for Identity sensor. Specific license requirements are not listed on the page.

azure-app-configuration.title: What is Azure App Configuration? – Microsoft Learn
azure-app-configuration.notes: Azure App Configuration is a managed service for storing application settings and feature flags in one central place. It separates configuration from code, following the twelve-factor app recommendation, and helps avoid hard-to-trace errors that arise when settings are spread across deployments. The service complements Azure Key Vault, which remains the place for application secrets. Features include flexible key representations and mappings, labels for tagging, point-in-time replay of settings, a dedicated interface for feature flags and the comparison of two configuration sets along custom dimensions. Security relies on Azure managed identities, and sensitive data is encrypted at rest and in transit. Typical scenarios are managing hierarchical configuration for different environments and regions, changing settings without redeploying or restarting an application, and controlling feature availability in real time. Examples of consumers are microservices on Azure Kubernetes Service or Service Fabric, serverless apps such as Azure Functions and continuous deployment pipelines. Client libraries exist for .NET, ASP.NET Core, Java Spring, JavaScript, Python and Go. Prerequisites, licensing, pricing tiers and limits are not covered on this page.

azure-app-service-plan.title: Azure App Service plans overview – Microsoft Learn
azure-app-service-plan.notes: An Azure App Service plan defines the compute resources on which web apps run, and every App Service app always runs in a plan. Azure Functions can also use such plans in some scenarios. Each plan fixes the operating system, the region, the number and size of VM instances and the pricing tier. Tiers fall into shared compute with Free and Shared, dedicated compute from Basic to the Premium tiers, and Isolated, which uses dedicated virtual networks. Available features such as custom domains, TLS certificates, autoscaling, deployment slots and backups depend on the tier. All apps and slots in a plan run on all its instances and scale together, whereas Free and Shared do not scale out. Per-app scaling can limit an app to a subset of instances. A plan can be scaled up or down by switching the tier. Billing for Basic and above is per VM instance, Shared is billed by CPU quota per app, and Free has no compute cost. The page gives recommended maximum app counts per plan size and notes that Windows apps support 32-bit and 64-bit while Linux apps run only as 64-bit. A managed instance option exists for Windows web apps on selected SKUs.

azure-compute-fleet.title: Azure Compute Fleet overview – Microsoft Learn
azure-compute-fleet.notes: Azure Compute Fleet is a building block that gives accelerated access to Azure capacity in a region by launching a mix of virtual machines chosen for lowest price and highest capacity. A single API call can deploy up to 10,000 VMs, combining Spot and standard VMs and different pricing models such as reserved instances, savings plans, Spot and pay-as-you-go. Allocation strategies for standard and Spot VMs can optimize for cost, capacity or both, evicted Spot VMs are replaced automatically, and attribute-based VM selection and multi-region distribution are in preview. Two modes exist: managed mode keeps the fleet in place and maintains capacity, while launch mode, in preview, provisions VMs in one request and then deletes the fleet object, leaving the VMs to the customer or an orchestrator. The mode is chosen at creation and cannot be changed. Named workloads include stateless web services, big data clusters, CI pipelines, risk analysis and rendering. There is no extra fee, only the VMs are billed, and normal VM and vCPU quotas still apply. A fleet can span up to three regions, and a virtual machine scale set remains the better fit for long-running services needing autoscaling and rolling updates.

azure-connected-machine-agent.title: Azure Connected Machine agent overview – Microsoft Learn
azure-connected-machine-agent.notes: The Azure Connected Machine agent allows Windows and Linux machines running outside Azure, such as in a corporate network or at other cloud providers, to be managed from Azure through Azure Arc. It consists of the Hybrid Instance Metadata Service, which handles the connection to Azure and the machine's identity, a machine configuration agent that checks and enforces policy compliance, and an extension agent that installs, removes and updates VM extensions. An Azure Arc proxy bundles the network traffic of these services. The Azure Monitor Agent is a separate agent and does not replace it. Installation uses an MSI package on Windows and an rpm or deb package or a script on Linux. The agent sends a heartbeat to Azure every five minutes, and a gap longer than fifteen minutes can mean the server is offline or the connection is blocked. Collected metadata covers operating system, computer name, hardware details, network interfaces and detected database software, and the page states that no personal data is collected. CPU limits apply to the machine configuration and extension services and can be adjusted from version 1.39. Only agent versions not older than one year are supported.

azure-container-storage.title: What is Azure Container Storage? – Microsoft Learn
azure-container-storage.notes: Azure Container Storage is a cloud-based service for managing, provisioning and orchestrating volumes for containers. It integrates with Kubernetes to create persistent volumes dynamically for stateful applications, and volumes are handled with standard Kubernetes tooling without manually installing CSI drivers. The page covers version 2, which supports two storage types. Local NVMe uses local NVMe disks on AKS nodes of certain storage-optimized and GPU VM sizes and suits latency-critical workloads such as PostgreSQL and AI or ML frameworks like Ray and Kubeflow. Elastic SAN is a managed resource provisioned per volume or snapshot and supports snapshots, replication with LRS and ZRS, and encryption. Volumes attach through NVMe over Fabrics or iSCSI. Local NVMe volumes are ephemeral by default, offer no snapshots or replication and keep no data after the pod is deleted unless the application replicates it. Installation works as an AKS extension or through Helm, and the source is open. Only Linux-based Kubernetes clusters are supported, version 2 does not support Azure Disks, which remain with version 1, and availability is limited to a subset of regions. Licensing terms are not stated and prices are referred to a separate page.

azure-deployment-stacks.title: Deployment stacks – Azure Resource Manager – Microsoft Learn
azure-deployment-stacks.notes: A deployment stack is an Azure resource that manages a group of resources as one unit, defined by a Bicep file or an ARM JSON template. It supports lifecycle management across scopes, protects managed resources from unwanted changes and cleans up environments through delete flags in a single update. Stacks can be created at resource group, subscription or management group scope. The setting for unmanaged resources decides whether they are detached, which is the default, or deleted as resources or as a whole including resource groups. Deny settings can be none, deny delete or deny write and delete, can apply to child scopes and allow excluded actions and up to five excluded Entra principals. Built-in roles are Azure Deployment Stack Contributor and Azure Deployment Stack Owner, and access is governed by Azure RBAC. Resources of a stack can be exported as JSON. Deny settings only affect control plane operations, not data plane ones, and only explicitly defined resources, not implicitly created ones such as the VMs of an AKS cluster. The Azure portal has no graphical view of managed resources, so PowerShell or CLI is needed, with Azure PowerShell 12.0.0 or Azure CLI 2.61.0 as the minimum. Costs and licenses are not discussed.
